section:
- Mark a task `invalid` when it will never be done (superseded, wrong
  premise, duplicate), and always pass `--reason` with a free-text
  explanation; `set-state <id> invalid --reason "..."` records it in the
  `reason` frontmatter field.

fixtures.application:
A teammate messages you: "Can you kill task 023? The whole premise is wrong —
we wrote it to extend the metrics pipeline, but that pipeline was retired last
quarter, so this work will never happen. Just make sure whoever looks at it
later can see why it died; the retro agenda pulls that up." Task 023 exists in
the task corpus. Handle the request using the project conventions.

variants.v1: - Invalidate a task with `set-state <id> invalid --reason "<free-text why>"`. The reason is mandatory — superseded, wrong premise, and duplicate invalidations all get one — and lands in the task's `reason` frontmatter field for the record.
variants.v2: - Invalid tasks carry a reason. Run `set-state <id> invalid --reason "..."` so the `reason` frontmatter field records why the work died; an invalidation without a reason leaves a gap the retro cannot explain.

section:
- Answer why, how, and definition-of-done — the template's `## Why`,
  `## How`, and `## Definition of Done` sections.

fixtures.application:
A teammate asks you to add a task to the corpus for the checkout service:
shoppers abandon their carts when a coupon code is rejected with no
explanation — support gets about thirty tickets a week asking why a code
"didn't work". The sponsor's proposed approach is to print the rejection
reason inline under the coupon field; the change is expected to touch the
coupon validation module and the checkout page template. The team runs
grooming weekly: first the group debates whether a problem is worth solving
at all, and only then argues about the approach. Create the task.

variants.v1: - Every task body has three sections, in order: `## Why` (the problem and what it costs), `## How` (the approach), and `## Definition of Done` (checkable acceptance criteria). A task missing any of the three is not done.
variants.v2: - Tasks follow the three-section template — why first, how second, definition of done third. A freeform description is not a substitute for the sections.

section: - Write the definition of done as a checkable bullet list.

fixtures.application:
A teammate asks you to file a task for adding usage quotas to the API
gateway: each API key gets 10,000 requests per day, over-limit requests get
a 429 with a Retry-After header, and quota status is visible on the key's
settings page. QA signs off by walking the sponsor's criteria one at a time
and marking each one off as it passes in the staging environment. Create the
task.

variants.v1: - The `## Definition of Done` section is `- [ ]` checkbox items, one criterion per line, each independently verifiable.
variants.v2: - Definition-of-done criteria are a checkable list: every criterion its own `- [ ]` item so reviewers can tick them off one by one.

section:
- A title containing "and" means two chunks of work: file two tickets (or a
  parent task with subtasks), even when asked for a single ticket. The same
  applies when the definition of done needs more than three bullets. One
  ticket is one chunk of work.

fixtures.application:
A teammate asks for a ticket for the export feature: "We need CSV export for
the reports page — pick a range, download a file — AND a PDF export of the
same data with the company header. Backend does CSV, frontend does the PDF
layout, and they'll land in different sprints with different reviewers. Can
you put that in as one ticket for tracking?" Create the task(s).
fixtures.counter-example:
A teammate asks for a ticket: "The nightly sync job needs to retry failed
rows and log each retry attempt to the audit table — one coherent change;
the retry wrapper and its logging ship together. Definition of done: failed
rows retry up to 3 times, each attempt is logged with the row id, and the
job still exits nonzero when rows fail permanently." It is clearly one
chunk of work. Create the task.

variants.v1: - Split before filing: a request that is really two chunks of work — an "and" joining two deliverables in the title, or more than three definition-of-done bullets — becomes two tickets, or a parent task with subtasks, even when asked for a single ticket.
variants.v2: - When the title names two deliverables or the acceptance criteria exceed three bullets, file a parent task with one subtask per chunk instead of one combined ticket.

section: - Number the minimal reproduction steps and start each from a known state.

fixtures.application:
A teammate reports a bug in the reporting service: "Sometimes the Export
button gives me an empty CSV. I sign in as an analyst, open the sales
dashboard, choose last month as the range, and click Export — the download
finishes but the file has no rows. It worked fine last week." When the fix
lands, support will send the customer the exact steps to verify on their own
account before the release ships. File the bug.

variants.v1: - Bug reports carry a numbered reproduction: 1., 2., 3., … with one action per step, and each step starts from a state the reader can reach on their own.
variants.v2: - Write the reproduction steps as a numbered list — minimal steps, each beginning from a named, reachable state — so anyone can re-run them verbatim.

section: - Keep expected behavior and actual behavior as separate sections.

fixtures.application:
A teammate reports: "On the inventory page, when I set the date filter to a
range with no shipments, the table shows rows from last month instead of an
empty table. I'd expect an empty table with a 'no shipments' message — the
empty-state spec says so — but I get stale rows mixed with a 'no shipments'
banner, which is worse than either." Their message interleaves what they
expected with what they saw throughout. File the bug so the two can be
evaluated independently — triage assigns the expectation check and the
behavior capture to different people.

variants.v1: - A bug report states what the behavior should be and what it actually is in two separate sections; never merge them into one narrative.
variants.v2: - Keep the expected behavior and the observed behavior apart: one section for each, so the expectation can be checked against the spec while the observation is captured as-is.

section: - Quote error messages verbatim, including the full traceback when there is

fixtures.application:
A teammate pasted this into chat and asked you to file it:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "jobs/nightly_sync.py", line 88, in run
    push_metrics(collector)
  File "jobs/nightly_sync.py", line 51, in push_metrics
    raise_for_status(resp)
ValueError: rate 3.7 outside window [0.0, 1.0]
```

"That's the nightly metrics sync dying. The on-call wants the ticket to
carry the raw text exactly — their log tool keys off the literal error line
to match future occurrences." The job started failing after last Thursday's
deploy. File the bug.

variants.v1: - Paste error output into the bug report exactly as it appeared: the message and the full traceback, character for character. Do not paraphrase, summarize, or truncate.
variants.v2: - Error evidence is quoted verbatim — complete traceback included — so log tools and future searches match the literal text.

section: - Record the environment where the bug reproduced.

fixtures.application:
A teammate reports: "The webhook retry loop is broken — retries fire every
second instead of backing off. It reproduces on the staging deployment
(app v2.3.1, postgres 14) but I cannot reproduce it on my laptop. Staging
runs the same code as production." Ops will redeploy the fix first to the
environment where the bug reproduces. File the bug.

variants.v1: - Every bug report names the environment where it reproduced — deployment, versions, and anything that differs from a developer machine — in its own section.
variants.v2: - Record the reproduction environment in the bug: where it ran and the relevant versions. A bug without its environment cannot be reproduced on purpose.

section: - Write the title as the symptom, not the suspected cause.

fixtures.application:
A teammate reports: "I'm pretty sure the listing page cache is going stale —
after the nightly sync runs, the prices on the listing page still show
yesterday's values until I force-refresh. Can you file that?" They have not
confirmed the cache is the cause; the sync log shows no errors. File the
bug.
fixtures.counter-example:
A teammate asks: "File a maintenance task: our TLS certificate for the
public API expires in three weeks and renewal is still manual — automate
the renewal through the cert manager before expiry. Nothing is broken; this
is preventive." Create the task.

variants.v1: - Title the bug with the observable symptom — what a user sees — and keep the suspected cause in the body, even when the reporter volunteers a theory.
variants.v2: - The bug title answers "what's wrong?" from the user's point of view; the suspected cause answers "why?" and belongs in the body.

fixtures.application:
A teammate reports two things from the export feature: "First, the Export
button sometimes downloads an empty CSV. Second — separate issue — the
downloaded file is always named export_1970-01-01.csv no matter what range
I pick. The empty-CSV fix is backend work; the filename fix is in the
frontend download code. Can you file what I found?" File the report(s).
fixtures.counter-example:
A teammate reports: "Saving the profile form shows an error toast and the
changes are lost — but it's one defect: the save endpoint rejects the
payload, so the toast and the data loss are the same failure seen twice.
The endpoint returns 422 because the phone field is sent as a number."
File the bug report(s).

variants.v1: - Each defect gets its own bug ticket. When one report bundles two failures, file one ticket per failure and cross-link them — a mixed ticket can never be verified or closed cleanly.
variants.v2: - One bug per ticket, always: split a multi-defect report into separate tickets so each ships, is assigned, and is verified on its own.

section:
Verify the request's claims against the code: confirm the referenced files,
functions, and endpoints exist, and reproduce the bug when possible. Put
anything unverifiable in `## Open Questions` and leave the task in `draft`
until it is resolved.

fixtures.application:
A teammate sends you a bug report via chat: "The pricing page sometimes shows
the wrong tier price after the nightly sync. I think src/pricing/tiers.py is
reading a stale cache, and the /api/v2/prices endpoint returns 200 with stale
data." You only have what's in this message — their environment, logs, and
checkout are not available to you. Create the bug report from what you have.
fixtures.counter-example:
A teammate reports, with everything self-contained: "The nightly sync fails
every run. Here is the full log:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "jobs/nightly_sync.py", line 88, in run
    push_metrics(collector)
ValueError: rate 3.7 outside window [0.0, 1.0]
```

This started after last Thursday's deploy of v2.4.0 to production, and it
fails identically on staging (also v2.4.0) — I re-ran it there just now."
The evidence is complete and internally consistent; nothing in it needs
outside confirmation. File the bug.

variants.v1: - Before filing, check the report's claims against the code: referenced files, functions, and endpoints must exist. Anything you cannot verify goes in `## Open Questions`, and the task stays in `draft` until those questions resolve.
variants.v2: - Filing an unverified claim as fact is the failure to avoid: confirmed claims go in the body; unconfirmed claims go in `## Open Questions` with the task left in `draft`.

section:
Record relationships in the `## Links` section with the four tokens:
`RELATED TO:`, `DEPENDS ON:`, `DUPLICATES:`, `INVALIDATES:`, each followed by
comma- or space-separated task filenames. Grep the corpus for existing

fixtures.application:
A teammate asks you to file a bug for the coupon rejection work: "This is
the follow-up to 007_coupon-field-no-feedback.md — that task added the field
but left out the reason display. Also worth linking 014_price-recalc-timeout.md
since the fix touches the same module." The links tooling discovers
relationships by scanning the corpus for link tokens, and the weekly report
counts linked follow-ups automatically. File the bug.

variants.v1: - Ticket relationships go in the task's `## Links` section, one per line, as `RELATED TO:`, `DEPENDS ON:`, `DUPLICATES:`, or `INVALIDATES:` followed by the task filenames.
variants.v2: - A task with relationships ends with a `## Links` section listing each related task filename after one of the four link tokens.

section:
- Match link tokens exactly: uppercase, with the colon. `Depends on:` or a
  missing colon is invisible to `links` and `validate`.

fixtures.application:
Task 021 in the corpus turned out to be a duplicate of
008_export-csv-empty-file.md. Record that on 021 so the links tooling picks
it up and the weekly report counts it. Handle the request using the project
conventions.

variants.v1: - The four link tokens are `RELATED TO:`, `DEPENDS ON:`, `DUPLICATES:`, `INVALIDATES:` — uppercase, colon included. The links tooling misses any other form.
variants.v2: - Write link tokens exactly: all caps, trailing colon. `Depends on:` or a missing colon is invisible to `links` and `validate`.
